papers.title: Integrative Transcriptomics and Machine Learning Nominate IL15- and PPP2R1A-Centered Programs in PTSD Using Pathway-Informed Autonomic-Cardiac Gene Prioritization.
papers.abstract: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is associated with immune and autonomic disturbances, but molecular programs linking PTSD-related blood transcriptional signals with autonomic-cardiac biology remain incompletely characterized. The public Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) cohorts analyzed here did not directly measure palpitations or autonomic dysfunction. Peripheral-blood transcriptomes from GSE81761 and GSE63878 were integrated with a prespecified pathway-derived autonomic-cardiac gene set constructed from Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathways. Genes overlapping the curated
papers.summary: This study integrated two public peripheral-blood transcriptome datasets from PTSD patients with a curated set of autonomic-cardiac genes derived from KEGG pathways, then applied machine learning to prioritize candidate genes. The analysis nominated IL15- and PPP2R1A-centered molecular programs as potential links between PTSD-related immune signaling and autonomic-cardiac biology. The findings are exploratory and require validation, as the original cohorts did not directly measure autonomic symptoms.

papers.title: AI-Driven Multi-Omics Approaches for Deciphering Small-Cell Lung Cancer Heterogeneity Using Nucleic-Acid-Based Features.
papers.abstract: Small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) is a rare but highly aggressive malignancy defined by rapid progression, early metastasis, and profound therapeutic resistance. Its extensive heterogeneity across genomic, transcriptomic, epigenetic, proteomic, and microenvironmental levels continues to undermine precision medicine. Emerging evidence highlights the complex role of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) alterations, histologic transformation from EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) to SCLC, and the influence of distinct transcriptional subtypes on clinical behavior.
papers.summary: This review examines how AI-driven integration of multi-omics data—genomic, transcriptomic, epigenetic, proteomic, and microenvironmental—can help dissect the extensive heterogeneity of small-cell lung cancer (SCLC). It highlights the roles of EGFR alterations, histologic transformation from EGFR-mutant NSCLC to SCLC, and transcriptional subtypes in shaping clinical behavior and therapeutic resistance. The paper argues that nucleic-acid-based multi-omics features analyzed with AI could improve precision medicine approaches for this aggressive malignancy.

papers.title: Biological rationales from language models enable leakage-resistant forecasts of target-indication success.
papers.abstract: Identifying which target-indication (T-I) hypotheses can translate into clinical success remains a central challenge in drug discovery. We present PRIORITI (Prospective Rationale-Informed Outcome Reasoning for Integrated Target-indication Intelligence), a leakage-resistant framework that separates upstream biological evidence synthesis from outcome prediction. Given only a target gene and disease indication, a domain-instructed large language model (LLM) synthesizes drug-agnostic human genetics across prespecified channels. These evidence were embedded and combined with static entity context d
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors introduce PRIORITI, a framework that uses a domain-instructed large language model to synthesize drug-agnostic human genetic evidence for a target-indication pair, then embeds this evidence for downstream outcome prediction. By separating evidence synthesis from prediction, the approach is designed to be leakage-resistant, avoiding contamination from known clinical outcomes. This enables forecasts of target-indication clinical success that are grounded in biological rationales rather than memorized trial results.

papers.title: AI-Based Comparison of UniProt annotations and Literature Across Human Kinases.
papers.abstract: Curated protein records and their supporting publications organize biological evidence at different levels of detail. Here, we used AI to independently answer a set of biological questions using either UniProt records or the full texts of the literature cited by those records, and then used AI-based evaluation to compare the resulting answers in terms of information coverage and semantic agreement. Fifty human proteins were selected from ten groups in a kinase sequence collection. Target-identity filtering retained 1,749 protein-publication records representing 1,655 distinct publications. For
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint uses AI to compare the information content of UniProt protein records against the full text of the publications they cite, for 50 human kinases. AI-generated answers to biological questions were compared for coverage and semantic agreement, revealing how curated database annotations and primary literature differ in detail. The work offers a scalable approach to auditing annotation completeness and consistency.

papers.title: Transformer-based decision support with CNN and ViT for prognostic risk stratification following adjuvant chemotherapy in high-grade glioma: a multicenter study.
papers.abstract: High-grade gliomas (HGGs) exhibit marked intratumoral heterogeneity, which is associated with variable survival outcomes among patients receiving standard adjuvant chemotherapy. Conventional methods relying on molecular biomarkers are constrained by technical limitations and tumor heterogeneity. This study aimed to develop a multi-channel 2.5D deep learning framework that integrates Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Vision Transformer (ViT) features to noninvasively stratify HGG patients based on expected survival outcomes following postoperative adjuvant temozolomide (TMZ) chemotherapy a
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.summary: This multicenter study develops a 2.5D deep learning framework combining CNN and Vision Transformer features to noninvasively stratify high-grade glioma patients by expected survival after adjuvant temozolomide chemotherapy. The approach aims to overcome limitations of molecular biomarker-based stratification, which are hampered by tumor heterogeneity and technical constraints.

papers.title: Nutrient Calculation Accuracy, Expert-Rated Clinical Appropriateness and Safety Indicators, and Reproducibility of Large Language Model-Generated Diet Plans for Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome: A Real-Case-Based Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study evaluated the nutrient calculation accuracy, reproducibility, and expert-rated clinical appropriateness and safety indicators of three-day diet plans generated for women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), recently proposed to be termed polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Methods: Anonymized data from six women with heterogeneous PMOS profiles, purposively selected from a single clinic, were converted into standardized Turkish prompts and submitted to ChatGPT-4, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Mistral 2.0 through free web interfaces. T
papers.summary: This study tested four large language models (ChatGPT-4, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Mistral 2.0) on generating three-day diet plans for six women with PCOS/PMOS, assessing nutrient calculation accuracy, reproducibility, and expert-rated clinical appropriateness and safety. It provides a real-case evaluation of LLM reliability for clinical nutrition planning in a specific patient population.

papers.title: Enrichment-Free Rare Cell Profiling in Pediatric Osteosarcoma Reveals a Circulating Cell Population Associated with Relapse-Free Survival.
papers.abstract: Outcomes for patients with osteosarcoma (OS) presenting with metastases at diagnosis or relapsed remain poor with five-year survival rate of only 20-30%. Risk stratification at diagnosis remains limited, and no validated prognostic liquid biopsy analyte currently exists for this disease. OS lacks the recurring mutational hotspots and epithelial surface markers that underpin liquid biopsy strategies developed for carcinomas, necessitating fundamentally different approaches to circulating biomarker detection.
papers.summary: This study introduces an enrichment-free method to profile rare circulating cells in pediatric osteosarcoma, a cancer lacking common epithelial markers and mutational hotspots used in standard liquid biopsies. The authors identify a specific circulating cell population whose presence correlates with relapse-free survival, suggesting a potential prognostic liquid biopsy analyte for this disease.

papers.title: MSCA-Mamba: A Compact Multi-Scale Mamba Network for Multi-Label ECG Classification.
papers.abstract: Objective: Multi-label electrocardiogram (ECG) classification requires modeling morphological patterns across different temporal scales and their sequential relationships while maintaining limited model complexity. This study proposes Multi-Scale Channel-Attentive Mamba (MSCA-Mamba), a compact architecture integrating multi-scale feature extraction, branch-wise recalibration, and state-space sequence modeling. Methods: MSCA-Mamba combines three parallel dilated Conv1D branches, branch-wise Squeeze-and-Excitation modules, and a unidirectional Mamba block. The model was evaluated on the PTB-XL d
papers.summary: The authors propose MSCA-Mamba, a compact deep learning architecture for multi-label ECG classification that combines parallel dilated convolutional branches, squeeze-and-excitation recalibration, and a Mamba state-space sequence model. Evaluated on the PTB-XL dataset, the approach aims to capture multi-scale morphological patterns and temporal dependencies while keeping model size small. This is a domain-specific architecture contribution for automated ECG interpretation.

papers.title: AIS-Informed and Land-Aware Eco-Routing for Maritime Decision Support Using Machine Learning and Metocean Data.
papers.abstract: Geospatial sensing and data analytics can support maritime risk and safety management by transforming vessel-movement and environmental observations into transparent evidence for route assessment. Within this context, reducing maritime fuel consumption requires routing methods that exploit historical vessel-movement data while representing geographical and metocean conditions explicitly. This study contributes an AIS-informed, land-aware eco-routing framework that integrates geospatial data processing, machine-learning-based fuel estimation, and weather-screening analysis to generate minimum-p
papers.summary: This study develops an eco-routing framework for maritime vessels that combines AIS vessel-tracking data, machine-learning-based fuel consumption estimation, and metocean (weather and ocean) data to generate minimum-fuel routes. The approach explicitly accounts for land boundaries and screens weather conditions, producing transparent evidence to support maritime decision-making and reduce fuel use.

papers.title: ATPPred: Prediction of Plant ATP-Binding Proteins Using ESM2 and 1D Convolution.
papers.abstract: Plant ATP-binding proteins play a central role in various physiological processes in plants, including growth and development, energy metabolism, signal transduction, and environmental adaptation. Accurately identifying ATP-binding proteins from plant protein sequences is crucial for a deeper understanding of plant physiology and their applications in agricultural biotechnology. In this study, we propose ATPPred, a tool based on the protein large language model Evolutionary Scale Modeling 2 (ESM2) and a 1-dimensional convolutional neural network for the high-precision prediction of plant ATP-b
papers.summary: ATPPred is a computational tool that predicts whether a plant protein binds ATP, using the protein language model ESM2 to generate sequence embeddings and a 1D convolutional neural network for classification. The authors report high-accuracy performance, offering a practical method for annotating ATP-binding proteins in plant proteomes without experimental screening.

papers.title: Explainable Machine Learning for Prediction of Future High-Severity States Using Longitudinal APACHE-II Trajectories: Internal Validation and Cross-Cohort Portability Assessment.
papers.abstract: Background: Longitudinal severity assessment may provide more informative risk stratification than reliance on a single admission score in intensive care. This study developed and internally validated an explainable machine learning framework for predicting a subsequent APACHE-II-defined high-severity state using repeated APACHE-II assessments in intensive care unit (ICU) patients receiving total parenteral nutrition (TPN). The endpoint was defined as an APACHE-II score of ≥ 20 at the final assessment (T10), while predictor information was restricted to measurements obtained at T0-T9. Methods:
papers.summary: This study developed an explainable machine learning model that predicts whether ICU patients on total parenteral nutrition will reach a high-severity APACHE-II state (score ≥20) at a later time point, using only earlier repeated APACHE-II measurements. The model was internally validated and its portability was assessed across cohorts, with explainability methods used to interpret which trajectory features drive predictions.

papers.title: Needle-Free Bedside and Anthropometric Measures Show Weak Discrimination of an Adverse Blood-Biomarker Profile in Middle-Aged and Older Mexican Adults: An Internally Validated Machine-Learning Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Needle-free measures such as grip strength, gait speed, and anthropometry are attractive as potential substitutes for blood-based biomarkers in low-resource settings, yet whether they can predict an adverse blood-biomarker profile remains unknown. This study aimed to determine whether machine-learning algorithms can predict such a profile from a defined set of needle-free bedside and anthropometric measures in Mexican adults. Methods: Using the Mexican Health and Aging Study (MHAS) 2012 biomarker subsample (n = 2000; mean age 62.4 years; 59.8% women), we defined a blood-
papers.summary: This study tested whether simple, needle-free measures (grip strength, gait speed, and anthropometry) could predict an adverse blood-biomarker profile in 2,000 middle-aged and older Mexican adults using machine-learning models. Despite internal validation, the models showed only weak discrimination, suggesting these bedside measures are poor substitutes for blood-based biomarkers in low-resource settings.

papers.title: A Drug-Referenced Machine-Learning Framework for Prioritizing Korean Herbal Formulations in Hypertension Using Linear SVM and Graph Convolutional Networks.
papers.abstract: Hypertension is regulated by interacting molecular systems, providing a rationale for network-based screening of multicomponent therapeutic candidates. Grounded in the conceptual framework of network pharmacology, we developed a hypertension-focused computational framework to prioritize insurance-covered Korean herbal formulations using protein-protein interaction networks derived from marketed antihypertensive and comparator drugs. Thirty reference-drug graphs (15 antihypertensive and 15 comparator drugs) were evaluated using four molecular classifiers under repeated group-aware nested cross-
papers.summary: The authors built a computational pipeline that uses protein-protein interaction networks from known antihypertensive drugs to rank insurance-covered Korean herbal formulations for hypertension. They compared four molecular classifiers, including linear SVM and graph convolutional networks, under repeated group-aware nested cross-validation. The work is a network-pharmacology screening framework aimed at prioritizing multicomponent herbal candidates rather than validating them experimentally.

papers.title: Prediction of Chemical Composition of Alfalfa Blocks Using FTIR Spectroscopy and Machine Learning Models.
papers.abstract: Alfalfa blocks are an important commercial roughage, and their crude protein (CP), starch, fat, neutral detergent fibre (NDF), and acid detergent fibre (ADF) contents are key indicators of nutritional quality. This study investigated Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy combined with machine learning for rapid quantitative prediction of these constituents. Different spectral preprocessing strategies and variable-selection methods were compared using partial least squares regression (PLSR), random forest regression (RFR), and back-propagation (BP) neural networks. The effects of spect
papers.summary: This study tested whether FTIR spectroscopy combined with machine learning can rapidly predict the nutritional composition (crude protein, starch, fat, NDF, ADF) of alfalfa blocks, a common commercial roughage. The authors compared spectral preprocessing and variable-selection strategies across PLSR, random forest, and BP neural network models, finding that model performance depends on these choices. The work supports FTIR as a fast alternative to wet-chemistry analysis for feed quality assessment.

papers.title: CYP1B1 is a potential target of kaempferol in renal fibrosis: a multi‑omics and single‑cell transcriptomics study.
papers.abstract: Renal fibrosis (RF) is a progressive and irreversible pathological process for which effective treatments are limited. This study explores the molecular targets and mechanisms through which kaempferol (Kae) ameliorates RF, with particular emphasis on cytochrome P450 1B1 (CYP1B1).
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics and single-cell transcriptomics to identify CYP1B1 as a molecular target through which the flavonoid kaempferol may alleviate renal fibrosis. The work links a natural compound to a specific cytochrome P450 enzyme in fibrotic kidney tissue, suggesting a possible therapeutic axis for a condition with few effective treatments.

papers.title: Cross-linking mass spectrometry guided structure prediction of disordered Encephalitozoon hellem proteins.
papers.abstract: Microsporidia such as Encephalitozoon hellem are obligate intracellular human parasites that remain genetically intractable, limiting the functional characterization of their proteomes. Experimental structural studies are challenging, as many proteins in microsporidia comprise a large percentage of disordered regions. Computational structural studies based on homology-based modeling and the use of deep-learning algorithms for microsporidian proteins also remain limited because most have little to no sequence similarity to proteins with solved structures. To address these limitations, we develo
papers.summary: The authors combine cross-linking mass spectrometry with deep-learning-based structure prediction to model disordered proteins from the microsporidian parasite Encephalitozoon hellem, which lacks tractable genetics and structural homologs. The experimental cross-link constraints guide and validate predicted structures, enabling structural characterization of proteins that homology modeling alone cannot handle. This provides a workflow for studying intrinsically disordered proteins in genetically intractable organisms.

papers.title: Digital image analysis-based quantification of p53 immunohistochemistry in gastric cancer: a systematic comparison of three-tier cutoff-derivation strategies in tissue microarrays.
papers.abstract: p53 immunohistochemistry (IHC) is a common surrogate for TP53 alteration, but in gastric cancer, its concordance is imperfect and depends on a non-standardized cutoff. Digital pathology enables H-score quantification, yet neither its reproducibility nor the choice of cutoff- derivation strategy has been systematically compared.
papers.journal: Journal of pathology and translational medicine
papers.summary: This study systematically compares three strategies for deriving cutoffs to classify p53 immunohistochemistry (IHC) results in gastric cancer tissue microarrays using digital image analysis and H-score quantification. It evaluates the reproducibility of these cutoff-derivation approaches as surrogates for TP53 alteration. The work highlights that p53 IHC interpretation in gastric cancer is non-standardized and that the choice of cutoff strategy affects classification.

papers.title: APR-Score: Identification and Scoring of Aggregation-prone Regions in Protein Sequences.
papers.abstract: Protein aggregation is a critical phenomenon associated with numerous neurodegenerative and systemic diseases. Understanding the propensity of proteins to aggregate is essential for unraveling the molecular basis of these disorders and for the design and engineering of novel proteins, as well as for modulating the activity/stability of enzymatic proteins. Here, we present APR-Score, a novel machine learning-based computational method designed to identify aggregation-prone regions within protein sequences. APR-Score leverages a combination of sequence-based features to predict regions of protei
papers.summary: APR-Score is a new machine learning method that identifies aggregation-prone regions within protein sequences using a combination of sequence-based features. It aims to help researchers understand protein aggregation in neurodegenerative and systemic diseases, and to support protein engineering and stability design. The tool provides region-level predictions rather than whole-protein aggregation propensity.

papers.title: PAZy: an expanded and actively maintained database of experimentally validated plastic-active enzymes.
papers.abstract: The Plastics-Active Enzyme Database (PAZy) is a manually curated resource for enzymes experimentally shown to act on synthetic or bio-based plastics. It was developed to distinguish experimentally verified plastics-active enzymes from computationally predicted or insufficiently supported candidates. Here, we present an expanded version of PAZy, implemented as a relational database containing >450 plastics-active enzymes with more detailed metadata, broader substrate coverage, and large language model-assisted curation of activity data. The redesigned web interface now enables browsing by prote
papers.summary: PAZy is an updated, manually curated database of over 450 experimentally validated plastic-active enzymes, now built as a relational database with richer metadata and broader substrate coverage. It uses large language model-assisted curation to extract activity data and offers a redesigned web interface for browsing by protein family and other criteria. The resource helps researchers distinguish truly verified plastic-degrading enzymes from computational predictions.

papers.title: Machine learning uncovers previously undetectable genetic deletions in cancer panel sequencing.
papers.abstract: Missed genetic deletions can prevent cancer patients from receiving effective targeted therapy. Standard pipelines, such as TSO500, use bin count averaging for copy number variation detection but often overlook focal events. To address this, we developed a machine learning (ML) pipeline for deletion detection and zygosity evaluation within the MASTERsg precision oncology program. We focused on the tumor suppressor gene PTEN, whose loss confers sensitivity to mTOR/Akt inhibition. An Extreme Gradient Boosting model trained on PTEN-deleted and wild-type tumor samples identified focal deletions mi
papers.summary: The authors developed a machine-learning pipeline to detect focal genetic deletions that standard copy-number pipelines like TSO500 miss in cancer panel sequencing. Focusing on PTEN loss (which can guide mTOR/Akt inhibitor therapy), an XGBoost model trained on deleted versus wild-type tumors identified previously undetectable focal deletions and evaluated zygosity. This could help more patients qualify for targeted therapy.

papers.title: Cross-domain signal grammars of transcription termination.
papers.abstract: Transcription termination establishes gene boundaries, recycles RNA polymerase, and prevents interference between neighboring transcription units. Termination depends on cis-acting elements, trans-acting factors, and the susceptibility of the elongation complex to pausing, cleavage, destabilization, or release. Predicted motifs, stable RNA ends, processing sites, readthrough regions, and polymerase-release regions are nevertheless often treated as measurements of the same event, which complicates mechanistic comparison and model development. This review compares termination signals as context-
papers.summary: This review argues that transcription termination signals across different domains of life are often conflated in the literature, with predicted motifs, stable RNA ends, processing sites, readthrough regions, and polymerase-release regions treated as if they measured the same event. It proposes comparing termination signals as context-dependent 'grammars' to enable mechanistic comparison and better model development. The work is a conceptual synthesis rather than new data.

papers.title: DeepNPA: A protBert-based framework for residue-level annotation of neuropeptide precursors.
papers.abstract: Neuropeptides are key signaling molecules that regulate the nervous and endocrine systems, and their maturation depends on precise proteolytic cleavage of precursor proteins. However, residue-level annotation remains essential yet experimentally labor intensive, with limited dedicated computational tools. Here, we present DeepNPA, a residue-level annotation framework that integrates ProtBert, a pretrained protein language model, with focal loss for imbalance-aware optimization. DeepNPA was trained and evaluated on a non-redundant Swiss-Prot-derived dataset annotated using the BIO scheme. On a
papers.summary: DeepNPA is a computational framework that uses ProtBert, a pretrained protein language model, combined with focal loss to predict residue-level annotations of neuropeptide precursor proteins, identifying cleavage sites and mature peptide regions. Trained on a non-redundant Swiss-Prot-derived dataset with BIO-scheme labels, it addresses the lack of dedicated tools for this experimentally labor-intensive annotation task. The work demonstrates how protein language models can be adapted to a specialized sequence-labeling problem in neuropeptide biology.

papers.title: Dynamic Fourier wavelet positional encoding for anticancer peptide prediction via transfer learning.
papers.abstract: Computational identification of anti-tumor peptides (ACPs) is challenged by limited training data and the multi-scale nature of biological sequences. Standard transformer positional encodings fail to capture the periodicities and local motifs that govern peptide function. We propose dynamic Fourier wavelet positional encoding (DFWPE), which replaces fixed sinusoidal encodings with parallel adaptive Fourier and multi-scale wavelet branches, fused by a context-aware gating mechanism. A dual-stage transfer learning strategy pre-trains on 5,785 curated peptide sequences before fine-tuning on ACP74
papers.summary: The authors introduce a new positional encoding method, dynamic Fourier wavelet positional encoding (DFWPE), for transformer models that better captures periodic patterns and local motifs in peptide sequences. Combined with a two-stage transfer learning approach, this method improves prediction of anticancer peptides, addressing challenges of limited training data and multi-scale sequence features.

papers.title: Cellular scaling laws in the mammalian brain.
papers.abstract: Recent whole-brain cell atlases have uncovered a consistent cytoarchitectural feature: the greatest diversity of discrete neuronal cell types resides not in the regions with the most neurons (e.g., the cortex and cerebellum) but rather in deep subcortical structures like the hypothalamus and brain stem. We propose that this discrepancy reflects a fundamental algorithmic division in the vertebrate brain between a "learning subsystem" and a "steering subsystem." The learning subsystem (cortex, striatum, and cerebellum) scales via the replication of repetitive modules to maximize computational ca
papers.summary: Whole-brain cell atlases reveal that neuronal cell-type diversity is highest in deep subcortical regions like the hypothalamus and brain stem, not in neuron-rich areas such as cortex and cerebellum. The authors propose this reflects a fundamental division between a 'learning subsystem' (cortex, striatum, cerebellum) that scales by replicating repetitive modules, and a 'steering subsystem' with greater cell-type diversity.

papers.title: Beyond prediction: The evolving role of artificial intelligence in genome editing.
papers.abstract: Since the discovery of the clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeat (CRISPR)-associated (Cas) system, genome-editing technologies have advanced rapidly, and the field has expanded substantially. In parallel, artificial intelligence (AI) has progressed at an unprecedented pace and is transforming genetic engineering. Early AI applications primarily addressed predictive tasks, including guide RNA (gRNA) activity, off-target effects, and editing outcomes for CRISPR-Cas nucleases, base editors, and prime editors. Recently, transformer-based protein language models (PLMs) and genera
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence is moving beyond simply predicting CRISPR editing outcomes (such as guide RNA activity and off-target effects) toward actively designing and engineering genome-editing tools. It highlights transformer-based protein language models and generative approaches as emerging drivers of this shift, positioning AI as a design partner rather than just a predictor.

papers.title: CLEAN Database: providing enzyme function coverage for over 55 million sequences.
papers.abstract: Enzyme function annotation is critical for decoding biological systems and enabling rational enzyme design. However, experimentally characterized enzyme functions remain available for only a small fraction of known protein sequences, resulting in a widening gap between rapidly expanding sequence space and reliable functional assignments. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have accelerated enzyme function annotation by facilitating accurate and high-throughput prediction from protein sequences. Here, we present CLEAN Database (CLEAN DB), a comprehensive resource encompassing >55 mi
papers.summary: CLEAN DB is a new database providing enzyme function annotations for over 55 million protein sequences, addressing the gap between the vast number of known sequences and the small fraction with experimentally characterized functions. It leverages AI-based prediction methods to assign enzyme functions at high throughput, offering a comprehensive resource for enzyme annotation and design.

papers.title: scChronos: Hierarchical Temporal Context Learning for Missing Snapshot Prediction in Single-Cell Time Series.
papers.abstract: Single-cell time-series atlases provide discrete cross-sectional snapshots of continuous developmental processes, making missing-snapshot prediction essential for reconstructing trajectories and dynamic programs. However, destructive scRNA-seq profiling prevents tracking the same cells across time, yielding unpaired population snapshots and making missing-snapshot prediction challenging. Existing methods typically rely on explicit dynamical propagation or transport-based coupling between snapshots, which may ignore the statistical constraints of the overall population distribution and be sensi
papers.summary: scChronos introduces a hierarchical temporal context learning framework for predicting missing snapshots in single-cell time-series data, where destructive profiling yields unpaired population snapshots. Unlike existing methods that rely on explicit dynamical propagation or transport-based coupling, it leverages statistical constraints of the overall population distribution to reconstruct continuous developmental trajectories. This addresses a key challenge in single-cell developmental biology by enabling more robust interpolation of unobserved time points.

papers.title: Quantifying pollen and spore morphology using a language model.
papers.abstract: In a typical systematic paper, specimen morphology is described with natural language, and taxonomic specialists use glossaries of technical terminology to establish and communicate taxon concepts, using morphology to delimit species. Textual descriptions of specimen morphology are therefore foundational to biological systematics, but they also serve as a primary data source for studies of morphological evolution. Typically, researchers extract attributes of taxon morphology from descriptions and analyse them to quantify how organismal form has evolved. Focussing on fossil pollen and spores as
papers.summary: This paper uses a language model to extract morphological descriptions of fossil pollen and spores from natural-language taxonomic texts, enabling quantitative analysis of shape and structure. It demonstrates that NLP can turn descriptive systematics into structured data for studying morphological evolution.

papers.title: Development and Preclinical Evaluation of Novel STK3/4 Inhibitors with Anti-Obesity Potential.
papers.abstract: Obesity is associated with impaired adipocyte metabolism driven in part by mitochondrial dysfunction. Serine/threonine-protein kinase 3 (STK3) and STK4 promote mitophagy, leading to reduced mitochondrial mass in adipose tissue. Thus, inhibition of STK3/4 represents a potential therapeutic strategy for obesity and related metabolic disorders.
papers.summary: The authors developed and tested novel small-molecule inhibitors targeting the kinases STK3 and STK4, which promote mitophagy and thereby reduce mitochondrial mass in adipose tissue. Their rationale is that blocking STK3/4 could preserve mitochondrial function in adipocytes and serve as an anti-obesity strategy. The abstract describes preclinical development and evaluation of these inhibitors, though specific efficacy results are not detailed here.

papers.title: PrOMet: Accurate and Robust Metal-Binding Site and Type Prediction.
papers.abstract: Metal binding to proteins is crucial for many biological functions, yet the prediction of metal-binding sites and metal types remains underexplored compared to other biomolecular interactions. Despite advances in deep learning, computational methods have achieved limited success in this area; even the best-reported approaches reach only moderate localization accuracy on high-resolution crystal structures, and even worse when applied to medium-resolution data. We hypothesize that the main challenge lies in the nature of metal binding. While the putative sites span the entire protein surface, ac
papers.summary: PrOMet is a new deep learning method for predicting where metal ions bind on protein surfaces and which metal type binds there. The authors argue that the main difficulty is that candidate sites cover the whole protein surface while actual binding sites are sparse, and their approach improves localization accuracy over prior methods, especially on medium-resolution structures.

papers.title: Massively Multiplexed Photonic Chip With Cross-Channel Fusion For Harmonized Biosensing.
papers.abstract: Accurate, label-free analysis of complex biological mixtures is limited by poor multiplexing scalability and inconsistent responses across sensor samples. We introduce a transformative sensing platform that integrates large-scale photonic multiplexing with data-driven analytics to overcome these constraints. Our modular, affordable glass-chip whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) photonic architecture is designed to support simultaneous readout of up to 100 sensing channels comprising over 10 000 high-Q microresonators, exceeding existing multiplexing capabilities by more than two orders of magnitude.
papers.summary: The authors present a glass-chip photonic sensing platform based on whispering-gallery-mode microresonators that can read out up to 100 sensing channels containing over 10,000 high-Q resonators simultaneously, a multiplexing scale roughly two orders of magnitude beyond existing approaches. They pair the hardware with data-driven cross-channel fusion analytics to harmonize inconsistent sensor responses across samples, enabling label-free analysis of complex biological mixtures. The work is a hardware-plus-analytics contribution aimed at scalable, reproducible biosensing.

papers.title: Protein Language Models Identify Early Folding Residues as Critical Hotspots for Pathogenic Variants and Cancer Prognosis.
papers.abstract: Identifying the specific residues that initiate protein folding is critical for understanding protein stability and the mechanisms of misfolding-related diseases. However, the systematic, proteome-wide identification of these early folding residues (EFRs) has been hampered by both experimental and computational limitations. Here, we present LMEFold, a deep learning framework using protein language models (PLMs) to accurately predict EFRs from amino acid sequence alone. LMEFold outperforms existing sequence-based predictors on the Start2Fold benchmark (ROC AUC = 0.831), and its predicted scores
papers.summary: The authors present LMEFold, a deep learning framework that uses protein language models to predict early folding residues (EFRs) directly from amino acid sequence, outperforming existing sequence-based predictors on the Start2Fold benchmark (ROC AUC = 0.831). They then show that these predicted EFRs are enriched for pathogenic variants and are associated with cancer prognosis, suggesting that folding-initiation sites are functional hotspots relevant to disease.

papers.title: A self-supervised foundation model for large-scale zebrafish image analysis.
papers.abstract: High-throughput zebrafish screening generates large volumes of imaging data, creating a need for scalable computational methods that reduce dependence on manual annotation and repeated task-specific model development. In this study, we develop a self-supervised foundation model for zebrafish image analysis pretrained on more than 468,000 images from seven heterogeneous zebrafish imaging datasets spanning different developmental stages, imaging platforms, modalities, and experimental conditions. By learning a shared representation from diverse unlabeled zebrafish images, the proposed framework
papers.summary: The authors developed a self-supervised foundation model for zebrafish image analysis, pretrained on over 468,000 images from seven heterogeneous datasets covering different developmental stages, imaging platforms, and modalities. By learning a shared representation from diverse unlabeled images, the framework aims to reduce reliance on manual annotation and task-specific model development for high-throughput zebrafish screening.

papers.title: Interpretable CT-Based Radiomics for Prediction of High-Affinity Neoantigens Associated Immunogenic States in Advanced Hepatocellular Carcinoma Treated with TACE Plus Targeted Therapy and Immunotherapy.
papers.abstract: Objectives: To develop and validate a CT radiomics-based machine learning model for the noninvasive prediction of HANS status in advanced HCC and to investigate the prognostic and genomic characteristics associated with HANS status. Materials and Methods: This retrospective study included patients with advanced HCC treated with TACE-based triplet therapy. Patients were followed until death or last follow-up. Tumor tissue underwent whole-exome sequencing for HANS calculation, and arterial-phase CT images were used for radiomic feature extraction. A radiomics model (HANS-Rad), a clinical model (
papers.summary: This retrospective study developed a CT radiomics machine learning model to noninvasively predict the status of high-affinity neoantigens (HANS) in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma patients receiving TACE plus targeted therapy and immunotherapy. Tumor whole-exome sequencing was used to define HANS, and arterial-phase CT radiomic features were used to build the predictive model, which was then linked to prognosis and genomic characteristics. The work suggests that imaging-based radiomics could serve as a surrogate for neoantigen-related immunogenic states without requiring tissue sequencing.

papers.title: ProFormer: generalizable classification of single-cell and plasma proteomes using deep learning.
papers.abstract: Proteins are the main drivers of cell function and disease, making proteomics a powerful technique for biomarker discovery and defining cell identity. While current technologies can profile thousands of proteins and reach single-cell sensitivity, limited throughput restricts applications such as robust classification of large biological or clinical cohorts. To close this gap, we present a deep-learning (DL) approach for the direct analysis of mass spectrometric (MS) data, assigning proteomic profiles to sample identity. Specifically, we introduce the ProFormer, a transformer pipeline that clas
papers.summary: ProFormer is a transformer-based deep learning pipeline that directly classifies mass spectrometry proteomics data, assigning proteomic profiles to sample identities without requiring extensive manual feature engineering. It is designed to be generalizable across single-cell and plasma proteome datasets, addressing throughput limitations in large biological or clinical cohorts. The approach enables robust classification of proteomic profiles for applications like biomarker discovery and cell identity definition.

papers.title: Integrative Network Analysis and Machine Learning Identify Cell Adhesion-Related Biomarkers and Immune Heterogeneity in Allergic Rhinitis.
papers.abstract: Allergic rhinitis (AR) represents a highly prevalent inflammatory disorder of the nasal mucosa, but molecular indicators capable of capturing its disease-specific transcriptional features remain insufficiently defined. This study aimed to identify cell adhesion-related diagnostic biomarkers for AR and to investigate their immune relevance and molecular heterogeneity.
papers.summary: This study applies integrative network analysis and machine learning to transcriptomic data from allergic rhinitis patients to identify cell adhesion-related genes as candidate diagnostic biomarkers. It further characterizes immune cell heterogeneity associated with these biomarkers, suggesting that cell adhesion pathways may help explain disease-specific transcriptional features and immune variation in AR.

papers.title: Machine Learning in Dementia Research: Trends, Biomarkers, Prediction Goals, and Data Modalities.
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) is increasingly used in dementia research for diagnosis, early detection, prognosis, biomarker characterization, and disease phenotyping. This study aimed to provide a bibliometric and thematic overview of ML applications in dementia, emphasizing biological mechanisms, prediction goals, data modalities, collaborative networks, and emerging computational approaches.
papers.summary: This bibliometric and thematic review maps how machine learning is being applied across dementia research, covering diagnosis, early detection, prognosis, biomarker characterization, and disease phenotyping. It catalogs the biological mechanisms, prediction targets, data modalities, and collaborative networks that define the field, while highlighting emerging computational approaches.

papers.title: Empathy in the Soil, Agents on the Desktop: Why Plant Pathology Needs a Scientist-in-the-Loop AI Paradigm.
papers.abstract: Plant pathology faces a cognitive bottleneck caused by the growing volume of biological data. Addressing it requires a shift from passive chatbots to autonomous AI research agents that operate in Goal-Action-State cycles. Researchers can set up a local, desktop-based agentic framework that combines semantic discovery, LLM-Wiki knowledge synthesis, and in silico prevalidation, managed under a human-directed three-tier organizational model. Strict "Scientist-in-the-Loop" boundaries, which means that a human researcher sets the goals, reviews AI-generated output before it is treated as evidence,
papers.summary: This perspective argues that plant pathology is constrained by a cognitive bottleneck from expanding biological data, and proposes moving beyond passive chatbots to autonomous AI research agents that operate in Goal-Action-State cycles. The authors describe a local, desktop-based agentic framework combining semantic discovery, LLM-Wiki knowledge synthesis, and in silico prevalidation, governed by a three-tier human-directed model with strict Scientist-in-the-Loop boundaries where researchers set goals and review AI output before it counts as evidence.

papers.title: Omics data discovery agents: Agent-supported retrieval, reanalysis, and synthesis of published omics data.
papers.abstract: The biomedical literature contains a vast collection of omics studies, yet most published data remain functionally inaccessible for computational reuse. When raw data are deposited in public repositories, essential information for reproducing reported results is dispersed across main text, supplementary files, and code repositories, and in the rarer cases where intermediate data (e.g., protein abundance files) are shared, their location is irregular. Here we present an agentic framework for the agent-supported retrieval, reanalysis, and synthesis of published omics data. The system employs lar
papers.summary: The authors present an agentic framework that uses LLM-based agents to retrieve, reanalyze, and synthesize published omics data from the biomedical literature. The system addresses the fragmentation of essential reproducibility information across main text, supplements, and code repositories, aiming to make published omics data computationally reusable.

papers.title: DNA augmentations for semi-supervised learning in genomic sequence classification.
papers.abstract: Semi-supervised learning (SSL) is a natural fit for genomics, where unlabeled sequences are abundant but high-quality labels are scarce due to costly curation. However, most SSL pipelines rely on generic perturbations that are not tailored to biological constraints, and it remains unclear which augmentation designs yield reliable gains for DNA sequence classification. In this application note, we present an empirical study of genome-aware weak-strong augmentation recipes for pseudo-label-based SSL, focusing on FixMatch and FlexMatch with a GROVER DNA language model backbone. Across two classif
papers.summary: This study empirically evaluates genome-aware weak-strong augmentation strategies for semi-supervised learning (SSL) in DNA sequence classification, using FixMatch and FlexMatch with a GROVER DNA language model backbone. The authors find that augmentation designs tailored to biological constraints can yield more reliable gains than generic perturbations, though the abstract is truncated before reporting full results. The work provides practical guidance on which augmentation recipes are effective for pseudo-label-based SSL in genomics.

papers.title: Integration of hereditary thrombophilia data and polygenic risk scores into prognostic models improves differential diagnosis of CTEPH.
papers.abstract: Differential diagnosis between pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) is crucial for treatment selection, particularly regarding surgical intervention. The prevalence of hereditary thrombophilias in Russian CTEPH patients and the utility of genetic data in differential diagnosis remain understudied.
papers.summary: This study examines the prevalence of hereditary thrombophilia variants in Russian patients with CTEPH and tests whether integrating genetic thrombophilia data and polygenic risk scores into prognostic models improves discrimination between CTEPH and PAH. The authors report that adding these genetic components to clinical models enhances differential diagnosis, which matters because CTEPH is surgically treatable while PAH is not.

papers.title: Machine learning-derived R-loop-related diagnostic signature for psoriasis: a multi-cohort and single-cell validation study.
papers.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease characterized by dysregulated immune responses and keratinocyte (KC) hyperproliferation. Although therapeutic strategies have advanced considerably, achieving durable long-term remission remains challenging. R-loops are three-stranded nucleic acid structures involved in genomic stability and inflammatory regulation in multiple diseases; however, their role in psoriasis remains poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning to build a diagnostic gene signature based on R-loop-related genes for psoriasis, then validates it across multiple patient cohorts and at single-cell resolution. It is among the first to link R-loop biology to psoriasis, suggesting these DNA-RNA hybrid structures may contribute to the disease's inflammatory and proliferative features.

papers.title: Mechanism of luteolin in treating chronic heart failure by regulating HIF-1 signaling pathway-mediated mitochondrial damage to inhibit cardiomyocyte apoptosis.
papers.abstract: Chronic heart failure (CHF) is a systemic cardiovascular disease characterized by an extremely poor prognosis. Luteolin demonstrates promising therapeutic potential in the prevention and management of CHF. This study aims to explore the mechanism by which luteolin ameliorates CHF through mitigating mitochondrial damage and inhibiting cardiomyocyte apoptosis, using bioinformatics analysis combined with in vitro and in vivo experiments.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study investigates how luteolin, a plant flavonoid, protects against chronic heart failure by targeting the HIF-1 signaling pathway to reduce mitochondrial damage and cardiomyocyte apoptosis. Using bioinformatics plus in vitro and in vivo experiments, the authors link luteolin's cardioprotective effects to suppression of HIF-1-mediated mitochondrial injury and apoptosis.

papers.title: Integrated transcriptome and single-cell RNA sequencing identifies transient receptor potential channel-related biomarkers in ulcerative colitis.
papers.abstract: The precise cause of ulcerative colitis (UC) is still unclear. While transient receptor potential (TRP) ion channels are increasingly linked to UC pathophysiology, the comprehensive roles of TRP channel-related genes are not well understood. This study aimed to systematically identify TRP channel-related biomarkers and develop novel diagnostic and therapeutic targets for UC.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk transcriptome data with single-cell RNA sequencing to systematically identify transient receptor potential (TRP) channel-related genes as candidate biomarkers for ulcerative colitis. The authors propose these genes as potential diagnostic and therapeutic targets, though the abstract does not report specific validated findings.

papers.title: Reduced hepatic GLUL expression accompanies altered RIP3/MLKL-pathway protein abundance in early cholestatic liver injury following bile duct ligation.
papers.abstract: Obstructive cholestasis is characterized by disturbances in bile acid homeostasis, amino acid metabolism, inflammatory responses, and hepatocellular injury. Although RIP3/MLKL-pathway proteins have been implicated in cholestatic liver damage, their relationship with metabolic alterations remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify necroptosis-related genes and associated metabolic-pathway alterations in early bile duct ligation (BDL)-induced cholestatic liver injury through integrated bioinformatics analyses and experimental validation.
papers.summary: This study uses integrated bioinformatics and experimental validation to show that early cholestatic liver injury after bile duct ligation is accompanied by reduced hepatic expression of GLUL (glutamine synthetase) and altered abundance of RIP3/MLKL necroptosis-pathway proteins. The findings link metabolic dysregulation, particularly amino acid metabolism, with necroptotic signaling in obstructive cholestasis.

papers.title: Immune and inflammatory features associated with pyroptosis- and myocardial fibrosis-related genes in HFpEF: a machine learning study.
papers.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a heterogeneous syndrome marked by inflammation, immune dysregulation, and myocardial fibrosis. Whether pyroptosis intersects with fibrotic remodeling in HFpEF remains uncertain. Two murine cardiac transcriptomic datasets were integrated after batch correction and intersected with curated pyroptosis- and myocardial fibrosis-related gene sets. Functional enrichment, univariate logistic regression, support vector machine-recursive feature elimination (SVM-RFE), and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression were us
papers.summary: This study integrated two mouse cardiac transcriptomic datasets and intersected them with curated pyroptosis and myocardial fibrosis gene sets to identify shared molecular features in HFpEF. Using machine learning (SVM-RFE and LASSO), the authors pinpointed candidate genes linking pyroptotic cell death to fibrotic remodeling and characterized associated immune and inflammatory signatures. The work suggests that pyroptosis-fibrosis crosstalk may contribute to HFpEF pathophysiology and highlights potential biomarker or therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Machine learning method for optimizing coding sequences in mammalian cells.
papers.abstract: Mammalian cell lines are the preferred hosts for producing commercially relevant therapeutic proteins such as antibodies, antibody derivatives, and cytokine fusion proteins. Even though significant investment is made to optimize upstream and downstream processes, the optimal gene design parameters for heterologous recombinant protein expression remain poorly understood. We describe a generic approach to gene optimization in which design features are systematically sampled and iteratively modulated using machine learning (ML). Synthetic gene variants encoding the Dasher fluorescent protein, dif
papers.summary: The authors present a machine learning approach to optimize coding sequences for heterologous protein expression in mammalian cells, using the Dasher fluorescent protein as a test case. By systematically sampling design features and iteratively modulating them with ML, they identify gene variants with improved expression. This provides a generic framework for gene optimization beyond traditional heuristic rules.

papers.title: Population-specific transcriptomic shifts underlie secondary metabolic diversification in Aspergillus flavus Link and the domestication of Aspergillus oryzae (Ahlb.).
papers.abstract: The genomic signatures of microbial domestication remain poorly understood within the context of natural population variation. Here, we demonstrate that Aspergillus oryzae, the filamentous fungus used in soy sauce and sake production, shares more recent ancestry with a predominantly northern, largely non-aflatoxigenic population of Aspergillus flavus (population C). A. oryzae isolates also overlap with the recently described, clinically enriched A. flavus population D, suggesting multiple domestication events. All isolates tested retained pathogenicity in a zebrafish infection model. At the tr
papers.summary: This study shows that the domesticated fungus Aspergillus oryzae, used in soy sauce and sake production, is most closely related to a northern, largely non-aflatoxigenic population of the wild species A. flavus, with evidence pointing to multiple domestication events. Population-specific shifts in gene expression underlie diversification of secondary metabolism between these groups, and all tested isolates remained pathogenic in a zebrafish infection model. The work links natural population variation to the genomic signatures of microbial domestication.

papers.title: Identification of active sequences in HIV-1 molecular transmission networks using machine learning: a cross-sectional study in Hainan Province, south China.
papers.abstract: New HIV-1 infections continue to increase in Hainan Province, a major tourist destination in southern China characterized by high population mobility and diverse viral subtypes. Understanding transmission dynamics within molecular networks is critical for precision prevention.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study applies machine learning to HIV-1 molecular transmission network data from Hainan Province, China, to identify which network sequences are actively transmitting. The approach aims to distinguish active transmission clusters from non-active ones, supporting more targeted prevention efforts in a high-mobility tourist region with diverse viral subtypes.

papers.title: Engineering a hemoglobin variant with enhanced stability and oxygen affinity using a protein language model.
papers.abstract: Engineered hemoglobin variants offer therapeutic promise for artificial blood substitutes and oxygen therapeutics, but rational design is constrained by protein stability and heme-binding. Protein language models (pLMs) predict mutation fitness, yet their integration with biophysical validation remains limited.
papers.summary: The authors use a protein language model to design hemoglobin variants with improved stability and oxygen affinity, then validate the top candidates experimentally. This work demonstrates that pLM-guided mutation prediction can be paired with biophysical assays to engineer oxygen-carrying proteins, a step toward artificial blood substitutes.

papers.title: AIPFusion-Net: an interaction-fusion framework for anti-inflammatory peptide prediction using protein language model embeddings, local sequence patterns, and handcrafted descriptors.
papers.abstract: Anti-inflammatory peptides (AIPs) are promising candidates for treating inflammatory diseases. However, experimental identification is time-consuming and costly, creating a need for accurate computational prediction methods.
papers.summary: The authors present AIPFusion-Net, a computational framework that predicts anti-inflammatory peptides by fusing protein language model embeddings, local sequence patterns, and handcrafted descriptors. This multi-view fusion approach aims to improve identification of AIPs over single-feature methods, addressing the high cost of experimental screening.

papers.title: Characterization and clustering of immunocompetent proteins based on ESM-2 sequence embedding and physicochemical feature fusion.
papers.abstract: Traditional sequence-comparison methods face challenges when classifying and identifying low-homology proteins formed by convergent evolution. In this exploratory study, we built a PCA-based unsupervised clustering workflow combining high-dimensional embeddings from the frozen pre-trained protein-language model ESM-2 and weighted-fused physicochemical features. The workflow was explored for family-level grouping, identification of putative functional conservation, and cross-species evolutionary analysis of immune-active proteins. An independent external test dataset was further used to prelimi
papers.summary: The authors built an unsupervised clustering workflow that combines ESM-2 protein language model embeddings with physicochemical features to group immunocompetent proteins, aiming to handle low-homology proteins that traditional sequence comparison struggles with. They explored the approach for family-level grouping, putative functional conservation, and cross-species evolutionary analysis, with a preliminary external test set. The work is exploratory and does not establish a validated classification method.

papers.title: Integrated computation-guided thermostabilization of the fungal sweet protein Honey Truffle Sweetener.
papers.abstract: Thermostability limits the use of sweet proteins as sugar substitutes in thermally processed foods. Here, we report an integrated computation-guided workflow for thermostabilizing Honey Truffle Sweetener (HTS), a recently identified fungal sweet protein with low intrinsic stability. We determined the HTS crystal structure and used it to guide subsequent computational analyses. Rosetta and ThermoMPNN evaluated candidate substitutions from complementary physics-based and deep-learning-based perspectives, and the selected single-mutant library was experimentally characterized. The resulting melti
papers.summary: The authors determined the crystal structure of Honey Truffle Sweetener, a fungal sweet protein with poor heat stability, and used it to guide computational mutation design. Combining physics-based (Rosetta) and deep-learning (ThermoMPNN) predictions, they built and experimentally tested a single-mutant library, identifying variants with improved melting temperatures. This provides a general workflow for engineering thermostable sweet proteins for use in processed foods.

papers.title: RCSB PDB AI Help Desk: retrieval-augmented generation for protein structure deposition support.
papers.abstract: Structural biologists have contributed more than 260 000 experimentally determined three-dimensional structures of biological macromolecules to the Protein Data Bank. Incoming depositions are validated and biocurated by approximately 20 expert biocurators at the collaborating data centers worldwide. Biocurators at the Research Collaboratory for Structural Bioinformatics Protein Data Bank, who process more than 40% of global depositions, face growing difficulty sustaining efficient Help Desk operations, having received roughly 19 000 depositor messages across some 8000 entries in 2025.
papers.summary: The RCSB PDB developed an AI Help Desk using retrieval-augmented generation to assist structural biologists depositing structures into the Protein Data Bank. The system aims to help the ~20 expert biocurators handle the growing volume of depositor questions—roughly 19,000 messages across 8,000 entries in 2025—by automating responses grounded in PDB documentation and knowledge. This addresses a scaling challenge in biocuration support for one of the largest structural biology data resources.

papers.title: An evidence-weighted knowledge framework with path-aware reasoning for personalized lifestyle management in chronic disease.
papers.abstract: Healthy lifestyle management is essential for chronic disease prevention and long-term care. However, evidence linking lifestyle behaviors, biological mechanisms, and health outcomes is dispersed across diverse biomedical sources. This fragmentation makes it difficult for health professionals to efficiently retrieve and interpret evidence needed to inform personalized lifestyle guidance.
papers.summary: The authors propose an evidence-weighted knowledge framework that integrates fragmented biomedical evidence linking lifestyle behaviors, biological mechanisms, and health outcomes, and adds path-aware reasoning to support personalized lifestyle recommendations for chronic disease management. The work addresses the challenge of retrieving and interpreting dispersed evidence for clinical decision support.

papers.title: Multi-omics graph attention network reveals neuro-immune-tumor pathways in breast cancer liver depression syndrome.
papers.abstract: Liver depression syndrome (LDS) is a core Chinese medicine (CM) syndrome implicated in the onset and progression of breast cancer, whose molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood, hindering further investigation.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with a graph attention network to uncover molecular pathways linking liver depression syndrome (a traditional Chinese medicine concept) to breast cancer progression, focusing on neuro-immune-tumor interactions. The authors identify candidate pathways connecting psychological/neuroendocrine factors with immune and tumor biology, offering a computational framework for studying CM syndromes with modern omics.

papers.title: GP-DHT: A dual-head transformer with supervised contrastive learning for shared-gene pretraining and single-cell GRN prediction.
papers.abstract: Gene Regulatory Networks (GRNs) are crucial for understanding cell fate decisions and disease mechanisms. However, inferring GRNs from single-cell RNA sequencing remains challenging due to noise, data sparsity, and species-specific distribution variations. We propose GP-DHT (Gene Pair-Dual Head Transformer), a single-cell GRN inference framework that pre-trains gene representations on a unified shared gene space using the BEELINE datasets of humans and mice. It models gene-cell expression relationships through a multi-relational heterograph and predicts transcription factor (TF)-target regulat
papers.summary: GP-DHT is a dual-head transformer framework that pre-trains gene representations on a unified shared gene space across human and mouse BEELINE datasets, then uses supervised contrastive learning and a multi-relational heterograph to predict transcription factor–target regulatory links from single-cell RNA-seq. The approach aims to overcome noise, sparsity, and species-specific distribution shifts that hamper GRN inference.
